question: Does staged verification and prioritisation retain important research findings beyond one pass, and does supplying audited analyses remove calculation/base errors on three orthogonal new studies?

cap.technical_retry_policy: Preserve failed attempts; at most one replacement for transport/runtime failure, no retries for poor research content.

inputs: Same public questionnaire, codebook and brief in each arm; approved numerical tables OR raw respondents. Both arms receive the same declared inference and denominator policy. All material hash-bound. No author/generator/hidden/reference/score files.
workflow: Existing pilot_runner.py TASK/STAGES unchanged except expanding study ID choices; each stage fresh context with prior output and same public files.
scoring: Existing frozen 1.1 semantic selection rules. Explicit full/partial/novel adjudication by Codex is provisional; no automatic topic-string matching or independent-human claim. M4 full credit requires both digital-attitude poles in a selected finding or narrative, not only intermediate analysis.
interpretation_limits: One replicate per arm is a capped workflow comparison, not E5 stability or a model ranking.
This is newly exposed development data, not a secret holdout.
Human validation and real-world transfer remain pending.
Costs remain unavailable when CLI reports only tokens; record null rather than invent dollars.
next_step: Blinded review pack and one evidence-bound approval-to-native-deck prototype per study, with QA approvals clearly marked as software checks.
